title: Statement registry (registry/1.0)

citationKey.$comment: 3 segments, fixed arity, no corpus-derived bytes. The paper coordinate is NOT here.

allOf.$comment: arXiv ids are immutable only WITH a version; the bare form resolves to LATEST and silently drifts.
textbook:<slug> sources carry no version axis; a version here is a category error.

kind_label.$comment: free per-topic label; the copier answer `frontier_kind_labels[]` is the allowlist mfc lint checks against

referent.$comment: The Mathlib or anchor constant this interface is claimed to model. REQUIRED for kind_class: interface unless no_referent is true. At near-zero Mathlib coverage a topic consists entirely of self-declared interface structures, every entry is one_way or no_claim, and statement_digest then detects drift in a private fiction while axes 1-4 and 6 all pass greenly. A named referent is the one cheap thing that makes `relation_claimed` relate to something outside the repo.

no_referent.$comment: An explicit admission that this interface models nothing external -- which is a legitimate state for genuinely novel mathematics, and must be SAID rather than left as an empty field. Requires referent_note.

referent_note.$comment: Why nothing external is modelled. Mandatory when no_referent is true.

declaration.$comment: The Lean declaration that discharges this item, and it must carry `@[discharges "<this item's id>"]` in the emission -- `mfc lint` E-12. Without it axis 6 was hand-edited YAML that mfc only aggregated: nothing checked the named discharger proves anything, so a discharge that existed only in prose was indistinguishable from a real one. This does not verify the mathematics; it removes the weaker failure.

allOf.$comment: kind_class: interface must either NAME an external referent or say out loud that it has none. Structural rather than a lint, for the reason R-01 and R-06 record: a schema constraint beats a rule a caller can skip. R-10 is the backstop for a caller reaching check() directly.
no_referent: true is an admission, and an admission with no reason is not one. Applies at every kind_class, not only interface.

chunk_id.$comment: CACHE HINT ONLY. Rotates on any parse change; there is no alias table and merge_insert has no delete arm, so a stale id stays addressable. Never authoritative.

matched_by.$comment: `fuzzy` is deliberately absent: an entry may not be MINTED on a fuzzy match.

corpus_version.$comment: LanceDB MVCC integer. Recorded, never trusted: a restore-from-backup presents a LOWER version over different bytes.

quote.$comment: The MACHINE-OWNED quote: byte-equal to the chunk body as the corpus produced it, and the only text `quote_sha256` is computed over. Do NOT correct a LaTeXML artifact here -- see quote_as_read. `mint_resolution.matched_by: quote_sha256` requires byte-equality with the chunk, so any human correction made here permanently breaks exact match and silently demotes the entry to printed_number (36 of 66 chunks even on the flagship paper) or to unresolvable.

quote_as_read.$comment: The HUMAN-OWNED quote: what a person read off the paper, with OCR and LaTeXML artifacts corrected. Displayed, never hashed, and deliberately not compared to `quote` -- they are supposed to differ, and the difference is the record of what the corpus got wrong. Null when no correction was needed.

quote_digest_source.$comment: digest_only mode: WHERE the hash came from, since the text is not inlined.

external_decls.$comment: Constants ALREADY IN MATHLIB (or the anchor) that this entry binds to directly. Emission is module-scoped to the topic library -- correctly -- so `@[cites]` can never be attached to `Mathlib.…`. Without this field a topic whose paper lemma is already formalized upstream must RESTATE it, and then the restatement's statement_digest, axiom closure and kernel replay describe the wrapper rather than the theorem, whose faithfulness to the paper is a different question from Mathlib's. Mathlib's own docs/1000.yaml solves this case in one line. Without it the architecture is useful only in the middle of the coverage range -- which is exactly where Bridgeland sits, and exactly why nobody noticed.

name.$comment: The fully-qualified constant name, as the emitter will look it up.

env_digest.$comment: The environment this binding was made against. A constant name alone does not identify a statement: Mathlib restates and generalises, so the same name at a later rev can be a different theorem. Pinning the env_digest is what makes `external` evidence rather than a hopeful reference.

mint_unresolved_reason.$comment: REQUIRED when mint_resolution is null. An entry that never matched a live chunk is legitimate -- an adopter with no corpus running, or an obligation with nothing to match -- but it must say which. A silent null is indistinguishable from a resolver that was never wired up.

allOf.$comment: verbatim mode MUST inline the text and MUST hash it.

A null mint_resolution must be explained. This is the schema half of the not_run discipline: 'nobody asked the corpus' and 'the corpus had no answer' are different facts, and neither may present as 'matched'.

$comment: QUOTE DIGEST GUARANTEE, stated honestly (#162): quote_sha256 is sha256(nfc-ws-collapse/1(quote)). It survives PREAMBLE-CLASS rotation -- an ingest that changes preamble_text and leaves body_text alone, e.g. ingest-recover-preambles -- and whitespace or Unicode-composition differences, which the normalization absorbs by construction. It does NOT survive a chunker bump: re-chunking changes chunk boundaries, which changes body_text, which changes this hash EXACTLY AS IT CHANGES chunk_id. The design's claim that it survives 'a chunker bump, an ar5iv re-render, a LaTeXML upgrade, an HTML-to-MinerU migration' was true of the first class only. What survives a merge or split is the quote_containment resolution rung, not this digest.
